selenium
Selenium is an essential trace mineral that functions as a cofactor for selenoproteins, playing a critical role in thyroid hormone metabolism , immune system support , and protection against oxidative stress via antioxidant enzymes like glutathione peroxidase.
The Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA) for most adults is 55 micrograms (mcg) daily, increasing to 60–70 mcg during pregnancy and lactation.
The Tolerable Upper Intake Level (UL) is 400 mcg per day ; exceeding this can cause toxicity, characterized by brittle hair, nail loss, and gastrointestinal distress.
Key dietary sources include:
Brazil nuts : The most potent source, with a single nut containing ~95 mcg.
Seafood : Tuna, halibut, sardines, and oysters.
Animal proteins : Organ meats, poultry, eggs, and red meat.
Grains and vegetables : Whole grains, mushrooms, and dairy products (content varies by soil quality).
